name: Hotel Cala di Volpe
positioning: Hotel Cala di Volpe, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Costa Smeralda: a seasonal Sardinian resort designed by Jacques Couelle, stretching over the bay of Cala di Volpe like a village, with an Olympic-size saltwater pool and a guests-only private beach
best_for: Design lovers drawn to Jacques Couelle's whitewashed, curving architecture
Beach and water-sports travelers who want a guests-only private beach
Families wanting a kids club for ages 3 to 12

facts.text: The hotel stretches out over the bay like a village.
The hotel overlooks the bay of Cala di Volpe, whose name means 'the cove of the fox'.
The hotel was conceived and designed by Jacques Couelle, who called himself a 'sculptor of houses' rather than an architect.
Couelle used the whitewashed Mediterranean style with curves, arches, spirals, picture windows and stained glass.
Rooms have handcrafted furniture painted to match each room's theme and ceramic tilework on the floors and in the bathrooms.
Rooms have a private terrace with views of land and sea.
The hotel has an Olympic-size saltwater pool by the sea.
The SHISEIDO Spa draws on Japanese savoir-faire and omotenashi, hospitality from the heart.
La Volpe Kids Club welcomes children aged 3 to 12, with an outdoor playground, gardening and children's cooking classes.
Calm waters allow paddleboarding and kayaking, as well as scuba diving and windsurfing.
The Mouratoglou Tennis Center Sardinia has tennis and padel courts with private lessons, group sessions and kids' programs.
Matsuhisa at Cala di Volpe serves Nobu-style Japanese cuisine by Chef Nobuyuki Matsuhisa.

highlights.text: The hotel appeared in the James Bond film The Spy Who Loved Me.
The hotel's private beach, reserved for hotel guests, is a five-minute boat ride from the hotel's private marina.
Rooms have whitewashed walls with trompe-l'oeil paintings, each one unique.
The Harrods Suite includes a bar, a wine cellar and a private infinity pool on a panoramic roof terrace.
The spa's Thermal Baths ritual includes a steam room, sauna, emotional shower and natural Sardinian scrubs.

considerations.text: The hotel operates on a season; the kids club, for example, is open daily during the hotel's season.
To explore the island further, guests would need a rental car.
A smart casual dress code applies at dinner in all restaurants and bars; shorts and beachwear are not permitted.
